info.title: Elody Collection API
info.description:
The REST endpoints every Elody deployment gets from **collection-api**, the service that stores and serves entities and mediafiles. This is not the GraphQL API the frontend talks to. A client can add its own endpoints and override these, so check your deployment for extras.

The examples use [the garage network](/example-domain).

**Base path.** Behind the standard ingress the API lives under `/collection/v1`. A local docker-compose setup serves it from the root of `collection-api.<domain>`. Every `/entities…` path is also reachable as `/elody/v1/entities…`.

**Authentication.** Send a bearer token issued by the deployment's identity provider (Keycloak by default) on every request, plus the tenant header (`X-tenant-id` unless the deployment renames it with `TENANT_DEFINING_HEADER`).

**Dry run.** Every endpoint accepts `?soft=1`: the request runs through authentication and the policies and stops before doing anything. A `200` means the caller would be allowed. The frontend uses this to decide which buttons to show.

**Concurrency.** When an entity type has an ETag key configured, `GET /entities/{id}` returns an `ETag`. Send it back as `If-Match` on `PUT` or `PATCH` to get `412` instead of overwriting someone else's change. Without `If-Match` the write goes through.

**Formats.** Single entities and filter results honour the `Accept` header: JSON by default, and `text/turtle`, `application/ld+json`, `application/rdf+xml` or `application/n-triples` for linked data. Filter results also come as `text/csv`.

servers.description: Example deployment; replace with your own host

tags.name: Entities
tags.description: Create, read, update and delete entities of any type.

tags.name: Filtering
tags.description: Search entities and mediafiles with a list of filter criteria. The filter language is documented in [Advanced Filtering](/services/elody-collection/advanced-filtering).

tags.name: Metadata and relations
tags.description: Change only the metadata or only the relations of an entity or mediafile.

tags.name: Mediafiles
tags.description: Files attached to entities: photos, invoices, manuals.

tags.name: Import
tags.description: Create or update many documents in one request.

tags.name: History
tags.description: Earlier versions of a document. Needs the history service.

tags.name: Jobs (internal)
tags.description: Job tracking used by Elody's own services (importer, transcoder, OCR). Not meant for integrations.

get.description: Returns a page of entities. Use `type`, `ids` and `q` for simple lookups and `POST /entities/filter` for anything more. Formats other than JSON need the `export` bulk operation enabled.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only return entities of this type.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: `key==value` equality filter on a key of the document. Repeatable.

post.description: Creates an entity. The type's validation and creation hooks run first. An array body creates several entities; the response is then the last one. Pass `current_job_id` to attach the new entity to a running job.

parameters.name: current_job_id
parameters.description: Job to attach the new entity to.

put.description: Patches several entities in one request; the body is read like an import, see `POST /batch`. Only present when the client enables the `edit` bulk operation.

delete.description: Deletes every entity in `identifiers` as a job. All are checked against the policies first; if any is forbidden, none is deleted. More than one identifier needs the `delete` bulk operation enabled.

405.description: More than one identifier, and the `delete` bulk operation isn't enabled.

post.description: Returns the entities that match every criterion in the body. A `type` criterion, or a `selection` on the `type` key, is required. The caller's access restrictions are added to the criteria automatically. See [Advanced Filtering](/services/elody-collection/advanced-filtering).

parameters.name: exact_count
parameters.description: `1` skips the count cap and counts every match.

work_orders_for_car.summary: Every work order on one car

get.description: Returns one entity. The `ETag` header is set when the type has an ETag key configured.

put.description: Replaces the entity with the body. Metadata and relations left out of the body are removed.

patch.description: Merges the body into the entity: only the metadata keys and fields in the body change.
Sets the metadata keys in the body on the entity. Keys the body leaves out keep their value.

200.description: The document's metadata after the change.

post.description: Adds the relations in the body to the entity. A relation with the same `key` and `type` as an existing one replaces it; the rest stay. In all three methods, relation metadata keys the body leaves out keep their stored value; send an empty value to clear one.

200.description: The document's relations after the change.

patch.description: Same result as `POST`: relations whose `key` and `type` appear in the body are replaced, all others are kept. In all three methods, relation metadata keys the body leaves out keep their stored value; send an empty value to clear one.

200.description: The document's relations after the change.

put.description: Replaces the entity's whole relation list with the body. Relations not in the body are removed. In all three methods, relation metadata keys the body leaves out keep their stored value; send an empty value to clear one.

200.description: The document's relations after the change.

get.description: Returns the mediafiles attached to the entity. Where the link is stored, on the entity or on the mediafile, and its relation type are set per client.

post.description: Creates a mediafile and links it to the entity. `relation_properties` becomes the metadata of that link. With `Accept: text/uri-list` the response is the upload URL for the file.

201.description: The created mediafile, or its upload URL.

relation_properties.description: Metadata for the link between the entity and the mediafile.

put.description: Makes the mediafile the entity's primary mediafile.
Makes the mediafile the entity's primary thumbnail.

get.description: Returns a page of original mediafiles; derived files such as transcodes are left out unless `q` says otherwise.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: `key==value` equality filter on a key of the document. Repeatable.

post.description: Creates a mediafile that isn't linked to anything yet. Usually you want `POST /entities/{id}/mediafiles` instead.

Returns the mediafiles that match every criterion in the body. A `type` criterion, or a `selection` on the `type` key, is required. The caller's access restrictions are added to the criteria automatically. See [Advanced Filtering](/services/elody-collection/advanced-filtering).

parameters.name: exact_count
parameters.description: `1` skips the count cap and counts every match.

get.description: Returns one mediafile. The `ETag` header is set when the type has an ETag key configured.

put.description: Replaces the mediafile with the body. Metadata and relations left out of the body are removed.

patch.description: Merges the body into the mediafile: only the metadata keys and fields in the body change.
Sets the metadata keys in the body on the mediafile. Keys the body leaves out keep their value.

200.description: The document's metadata after the change.

post.description: Adds the relations in the body to the mediafile. A relation with the same `key` and `type` as an existing one replaces it; the rest stay. In all three methods, relation metadata keys the body leaves out keep their stored value; send an empty value to clear one.

200.description: The document's relations after the change.

patch.description: Same result as `POST`: relations whose `key` and `type` appear in the body are replaced, all others are kept. In all three methods, relation metadata keys the body leaves out keep their stored value; send an empty value to clear one.

200.description: The document's relations after the change.

put.description: Replaces the mediafile's whole relation list with the body. Relations not in the body are removed. In all three methods, relation metadata keys the body leaves out keep their stored value; send an empty value to clear one.

200.description: The document's relations after the change.

get.description: Returns ticketed download links for the original and the transcode. Which links the caller gets depends on the client's copyright policy, so this endpoint needs a client policy that sets copyright access.

200.description: The links the caller may use.

get.description: Returns whether the caller may download the original file, as decided by the client's copyright policy. Needs that policy to be present.

post.description: Creates a mediafile derived from this one, such as an OCR result or a transcode, and links the two. Set `technical_origin` to what produced it.

409.description: OCR is locked for this entity.

patch.description: Asks the transcode service to build the mediafile's transcode again, as a job. Only works on original files.

post.description: Regenerates the transcode of every mediafile in `identifiers`, under one parent job.

Creates or updates many entities and mediafiles in one request, as a job. The body is parsed according to its `Content-Type` by the client's batch serializer, typically `text/csv` with one document per line. With `Accept: text/uri-list` the response is the list of upload URLs for the mediafiles in the import. Only present when the client enables the `import` bulk operation.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: `1` validates every row and writes nothing.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Name shown on the import job.

parameters.name: parent_job_id
parameters.description: Job to run this import under.

text/csv.example:
part_number,name,category,price,stock_quantity
BP-1042,Brake pad set front,brakes,64.50,12
OF-0331,Oil filter,filters,11.90,40

get.description: Returns the latest stored version of a document, the version that was current at `timestamp`, or every version with `all=1`. Needs the history service to be running.

parameters.name: timestamp
parameters.description: Return the version at this moment.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: `1` returns every version. Can't be combined with `timestamp`.

200.description: One version, or a list of versions with `all=1`.

get.description: Returns a page of share links.

post.description: Creates a job in the `queued` state.

post.summary: Finish a job with a warning
post.description: Finish a job with a warning.

post.summary: Link a document to a job
post.description: Link a document to a job.

get.description: Returns the job's status and info message.

bearerAuth.description: An access token from the deployment's identity provider, or a static JWT issued for a service account.

tenant.name: X-tenant-id
tenant.description: The garage (tenant) the request acts in. Required when the user has access to more than one.

id.name: id
id.description: Any of the document's identifiers: the readable id, the UUID, or another identifier the type registers.

orderBy.name: order_by
orderBy.description: Key to sort on, for example `metadata.planned_date.value`.

field.name: field
field.description: Return only these keys. Repeatable; `field[]` works too.

soft.name: soft
soft.description: `1` checks authentication and policies and stops there. See *Dry run* above.

ifMatch.name: If-Match
ifMatch.description: The `ETag` from your last read. The write fails with `412` when the document changed since.

BadRequest.description: The request is invalid, for example a body that fails the type's validation.

example.message: R0011 | id:WO-0000000 | collection:entities - Item with id WO-0000000 doesn't exist in collection entities

Conflict.description: A unique key is already taken by another document.

PreconditionFailed.description: `If-Match` doesn't match the current ETag: someone changed the document after you read it.

message.description: Starts with an error code, for example `R0011`.

value.description: A string, number, boolean, object or array, depending on the key.

lang.description: Language of the value, for multilingual keys.

metadata.description: Metadata stored on the relation itself.

id.description: Readable identifier, when the type has one.

identifiers.description: Every identifier the document can be fetched by.

technical_origin.description: `original` for an uploaded file, otherwise what derived it, for example `ocr`.

display_filename.description: The file to show: the transcode when there is one.

technical_origin.description: `original` for an uploaded file, otherwise what derived it, for example `transcode` or `ocr`.

filter.description: One filter criterion. See [Advanced Filtering](/services/elody-collection/advanced-filtering) for every type, matcher and option.

count.description: Total number of matches. Can be capped; see the filtering docs.

next.description: Relative link to the next page, when there is one.

previous.description: Relative link to the previous page, when there is one.

original_file_location.description: Ticketed link to the original file, when the caller may download it.

transcode_file_location.description: Ticketed link to the transcode. For PDF, XML and plain text this is the original.
